recent_posts.title: New Python Jumpstart course
recent_posts.summary: Trey Hunner has launched Python Jumpstart, a self-paced introductory Python course built around active learning through 46 short coding exercises. Rather than passive video watching, learners write Python code from the start. Each exercise is preceded by a short 5-minute video, and the course uses spaced repetition to reinforce concepts. Estimated completion time is about 7 weeks at 30 minutes per day. A launch week discount of 50% ($99) is available until December 2, 2024.

recent_posts.title: Using a ~/.pdbrc file to customize the Python Debugger
recent_posts.summary: You can customize Python's built-in debugger (PDB) by creating a ~/.pdbrc file with custom aliases. The post shares a practical set of aliases: `dir` to print non-dunder attributes and methods, `attrs` for non-method data attributes only, `vars` for instance variables, `src` to display source code and location of a class or function, and `loc` to list local variables in the current frame. Each alias formats output more readably than the equivalent built-in calls. Key limitations of .pdbrc are noted: aliases must be written on a single line, and variable assignments in aliases leak into the surrounding scope (requiring explicit `del` cleanup).

recent_posts.title: My favorite reads of 2025
recent_posts.summary: A Python educator shares their 13 favorite audiobooks out of 41 read in 2025, organized into three categories: world betterment (immigration, economics, sociology), self betterment (communication, cynicism, nutrition), and fiction (sci-fi, contemporary). Brief reviews and recommendations are provided for each book, along with a suggestion to switch from Audible to Libro.fm.

recent_posts.title: Tips for PyCon tutorial presenters
recent_posts.summary: Practical advice for PyCon tutorial presenters covering screen readability, active learning techniques, setup logistics, contingency planning, and classroom management. Key recommendations include using light mode with large fonts, building in frequent recall exercises, sending setup instructions well before the event, recruiting teaching assistants, using sticky notes for help signals, and mentally rehearsing the session to anticipate problems.

recent_posts.title: Default Apps of 2025
recent_posts.summary: A developer's curated list of default apps for 2025, covering tools for notes, coding, LLM usage, terminal setup, Python tooling, and productivity. Key highlights include NeoVim and Obsidian for notes and writing, Claude Code as the primary LLM coding agent, uv for Python installation management, Kagi for search, and a switch from Pocket Casts to Podcast Republic. Notable changes from 2024 include increased LLM usage via command-line agents and adoption of justfiles.

recent_posts.title: Why Congress should pass the End Kidney Deaths Act
recent_posts.summary: Trey Hunner, a Python educator, advocates for the End Kidney Deaths Act currently in Congress, which would provide $50,000 in tax credits (spread over 5 years) to non-directed kidney donors. He explains the kidney shortage crisis — over 100,000 patients on the transplant list, ~40,000 deaths per year — and how non-directed donations unlock kidney donation chains that save multiple lives. He addresses the ethical 'ick factor' around compensating organ donors, compares it to compensated plasma donation, and argues the tax credit approach is less exploitative than private markets. He encourages readers to contact their representatives and join the EndKidneyDeathsAct.org effort.

recent_posts.title: My favorite audiobooks of 2024 (and also 2017 through 2023)
recent_posts.summary: Trey Hunner, a Python educator, shares his favorite audiobooks from 2024 along with standout picks from 2017–2023. The 2024 highlights span nutrition, linguistics, urban economics, climate change, free will, and animal welfare. He also recommends avoiding Audible in favor of Libro.fm and Libby, citing dark patterns like expiring credits and app-locked purchases.

recent_posts.title: Handy Python REPL Modifications
recent_posts.summary: A guide to customizing the Python REPL using a PYTHONSTARTUP file and the pyrepl-hacks library. Covers setting up custom keyboard shortcuts (Home/End navigation, Shift+Tab dedent, Alt+Up/Down line swapping, and custom data insertion shortcuts), monkey-patching sys.path to make a shared package available across all virtual environments, and creating your own REPL commands using the bind decorator. The post also warns that these hacks rely on the undocumented _pyrepl internal module introduced in Python 3.13, which may break in future versions.

recent_posts.title: Which social network are we using for PyCon US this year?
recent_posts.summary: A look at which social network the Python community will use most during PyCon US 2025. Based on polls run across LinkedIn, Twitter, Bluesky, and Mastodon, Mastodon and Bluesky are the top contenders, with Twitter no longer the clear leader. The author predicts Mastodon will edge out Bluesky for #PyConUS posts, though the community remains fragmented across platforms. Recommendations include following the #PyConUS hashtag on both Mastodon and Bluesky and joining a PyCon US starter pack on Bluesky.
